subject.title: Improve read tool handling for binary document formats (.docx, .pdf, .pptx, .xlsx) & Avoid Token Waste on Binary Read

question: Should this issue be fixed as a narrow read-tool unsupported-document fallback, native core document extraction, or deferred to broader document/file-input architecture?
rationale: The source-reproducible token-waste problem is real, but the permanent boundary changes depending on whether read stays a text/image tool, learns safe document parsing, or delegates to provider-native/ClawHub document paths.

options.title: Narrow Safe Fallback
options.body: Add bounded PDF/Office MIME and extension detection in the read path and return a clear message instead of raw decoded bytes.

options.title: Core Document Extraction
options.body: Define parser dependencies, archive/XML limits, sandbox behavior, and tests before adding native Office/PDF extraction to read.

options.title: Defer To File-Input Architecture
options.body: Keep this issue linked to broader document extraction and provider-native file-input trackers until maintainers settle that architecture.

recommendation.title: Narrow Safe Fallback
recommendation.body: Add bounded PDF/Office MIME and extension detection in the read path and return a clear message instead of raw decoded bytes.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent Office-path, inbound-media, and document-extract commits make this the strongest routing signal for the read/document boundary decision.
